topStories.headline: Midlothian Holds Bond Townhall Tuesday Before $192 Million November Vote
topStories.dek: Residents can hear about five bond propositions — covering roads, a police substation, drainage, and parks — before the Nov. 3 special election.
topStories.body:
The City of Midlothian is asking voters to decide on five bond propositions totaling roughly $192 million on November 3, and it is giving them a public preview first. A townhall meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, October 13, at 5 p.m. at City Hall, one hour before the regular council meeting begins at 6 p.m. City officials will present information on what each proposition would fund and take questions from the public.

The five propositions on the November ballot are: Proposition A, $102.3 million for street and road improvements; Proposition B, $6.8 million to construct and equip a new police substation; Proposition C, $10 million for drainage surveys and improvements; Proposition D, $47.26 million for upgrades to existing parks; and Proposition E, $26.085 million to build new parks on city-owned land. The slate was recommended by a citizen planning and steering committee and the council voted 7–0 in August to call the special election.

Early voting for the November 3 General and Special Elections runs October 19 through October 30 at Ellis County locations. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Residents who want to weigh in before casting a ballot are encouraged to attend Tuesday's townhall; no registration is required and the meeting is open to the public.

topStories.headline: Red Oak Kicks Off Fall Saturday with Trash Bash Cleanup and Kids Fishing Event
topStories.dek: Two free community events run simultaneously Saturday morning — a bulk-item drop-off for residents and a youth fishing outing with first responders at Pearson Park.
topStories.body:
Red Oak residents have two reasons to head out early this Saturday, October 10. The city's annual Trash Bash runs from 7:30 to 10:30 a.m. at Oaks Church, 777 South I-35, in partnership with CWD. The event is open to Red Oak residents only and gives households a chance to drop off items that don't fit in regular curbside collection.

At the same time, the city's Parks and Recreation Department is hosting Fall for Fishing with First Responders at Pearson Park Lake, 200 Lakeview Parkway, from 8 to 10 a.m. The free event pairs kids ages 5 to 16 with local first responders for a morning of fishing on the pond. Registration is required; children must be accompanied by an adult and should bring a rod and reel if they have one.

Both events are free and designed with families in mind. Red Oak residents looking for additional fall programming can also mark October 17 on their calendars: the Red Oak Fall Festival returns to Pearson Park and the Municipal Center from 3 to 6 p.m., with live entertainment, rides, crafts, and candy.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Scarecrow Festival Opens for Entries This Weekend — Deadline Is Today
topStories.dek: The Midlothian Downtown Business Association's annual Scarecrow Festival runs Oct. 10 through Nov. 3 in Heritage Park, and entry forms were due by Oct. 10.
topStories.body:
The Midlothian Downtown Business Association's annual Scarecrow Festival is underway. Scarecrow entries may be installed at Heritage Park, 234 N. 8th Street, between October 10 and October 16, with the festival display remaining up through November 3. Entry forms were due by October 10 — today is the last day to submit one.

The festival theme is 'Halloween Fun.' Entry is free and open to individuals, families, groups, and businesses. Designs that are humorous or creative are welcome; entries depicting violence, vulgarity, nudity, or political messaging will be disqualified. Winning entries will be announced at Heritage Day on October 31, the Downtown Business Association's larger fall celebration in Historic Downtown Midlothian, which runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and features local vendors, family activities, and seasonal entertainment.

The scarecrow display gives downtown foot traffic a reason to stroll Heritage Park through Halloween, and organizers say it draws visitors from across the region each year.

moreNews.headline: Autumn Beats Concert Series Wraps Up November 7 with Private Orchid Band
moreNews.body: The City of Midlothian's free outdoor Autumn Beats concert series concludes Saturday, November 7, at 7:30 p.m. at Community Park's Art Pierard Memorial Amphitheater, 3601 S. 14th Street. The final act of the three-show 2026 lineup is the Private Orchid Band. Concerts are free and open to the public, sponsored by Midlothian Community Development and Texas Health Neighborhood Care & Wellness Midlothian.

moreNews.headline: Red Oak ISD School Board Meeting Set for October 19
moreNews.body: The Red Oak Independent School District Board of Trustees will hold its regular school board meeting on Monday, October 19, from 6 to 7 p.m. at 109 W. Red Oak Road, Red Oak. The district has been in the news this fall after its state accountability score rose from 77 to 78 in the 2026 ratings and the number of district academic distinctions grew from seven to ten.
